title: Ethiopian English Natural Stream Entrance 2018
description: Ethiopian English Natural Stream Entrance 2018 featuring 100 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText: Take an umbrella with you when you go out as it __________ rain later.
questions.explanation:
'Might' is used to express possibility.

 The sentence says that rain is possible later, but it is not certain.

 Therefore, 'might' correctly completes the sentence: 'It might rain later.'

questions.questionText: Profits have increased for the past six months; __________, we were not able to settle our financial position.
questions.explanation:
'However' is a linking word used to show contrast.

 The first part gives a positive situation—profits have increased—while the second part gives an unexpected negative situation—the financial position was not settled.

 Therefore, 'however' is appropriate.

questions.questionText: I bought my sister __________ mobile and a new book for her birth day. I don't think she liked __________ mobile.
questions.explanation:
'A' is used when a singular countable noun is mentioned for the first time: 'a mobile.'

 After the mobile has already been introduced, 'the' is used to refer to that particular mobile: 'the mobile.'

 Therefore, the correct combination is 'a/the.'

questions.questionText: Your travel record indicates that you have visited __________ countries.
questions.explanation:
'Countries' is a plural countable noun. 

The quantifier 'many' is used with plural countable nouns, while 'much' and 'little' are normally used with uncountable nouns.

 Therefore, 'many countries' is grammatically correct.

questions.questionText: The president of the university has given rewards for a few model instructors __________ motivate them.
questions.explanation:
'So as to' is followed directly by the base form of a verb and expresses purpose.

 Here, 'so as to motivate them' means the rewards were given for the purpose of motivating the instructors.

 'So that' and 'in order that' would normally be followed by a subject and a verb.

questions.questionText: She __________ her homework yesterday while her mother was preparing the dinner.
questions.explanation:
'Was doing' is the past continuous tense.

 It describes an action that was in progress at a particular time in the past.

 The action of doing homework was happening while her mother was preparing dinner, so 'was doing' is the correct form.

questions.questionText: The manager affirmed that all employees who behaved __________ could be allowed to attend the general meeting held at the Sheraton Hotel.
questions.explanation:
'Behaved' is a verb, so it needs an adverb to describe how the employees behaved. 

'Well' is the adverb form associated with 'good' and correctly describes their behavior.

 Therefore, 'behaved well' is correct.

questions.questionText: We heard a loud noise outside __________ we were visiting around the museum.
questions.explanation:
'While' is used to connect two actions that were happening during the same period of time. 

'Were visiting' is in the past continuous tense, so 'while we were visiting around the museum' correctly shows that the loud noise occurred during that activity.

questions.questionText: If everyone had a car, the roads __________ more congested than they are now.
questions.explanation:
This is a second conditional sentence used for a hypothetical or unlikely present situation.

 Its structure is 'If + past simple, would + base verb.'

 Therefore, 'If everyone had a car, the roads would be more congested' is correct.

questions.questionText: We were driving on the highway when we saw a car that __________.
questions.explanation:
'Broke down' is the past simple form and describes a completed event in the past.

 The sentence refers to something that happened while they were driving, so 'a car that broke down' correctly describes the event.

questions.questionText: In the factory, sand, soda, lime and crushed glass __________ together.
questions.explanation:
The materials 'sand, soda, lime and crushed glass' form a plural subject and receive the action of mixing.

 Therefore, the present passive form 'are mixed' is required. 

The complete sentence is 'In the factory, sand, soda, lime and crushed glass are mixed together.'

questions.questionText: __________ of the books available on the shelf were torn out and outdated.
questions.explanation:
'Some' is used with plural countable nouns when referring to an unspecified number or amount.

 Since 'books' is plural and countable, 'some of the books' is correct. 

The plural verb 'were' also agrees with 'books.'

questions.questionText: Many tourists visit the Semen Mountains Park, which is home for __________ animals, which are only found in Ethiopia.
questions.explanation:
'Endemic' describes a plant or animal species that is native to and restricted to a particular geographical area. 

Since the animals mentioned are only found in Ethiopia, 'endemic' is the correct word.

questions.questionText: She has decided __________ her boyfriend a special gift for his birth day.
questions.explanation:
The verb 'decide' is normally followed by the infinitive 'to + base verb.' 

Therefore, 'has decided to buy' is grammatically correct.

 The other forms do not follow the required pattern after 'decide.'

questions.questionText: Cotton __________ for thousands of years to make varied types of clothes.
questions.explanation:
Cotton receives the action of using, so the passive voice is required. 

'For thousands of years' connects the action with the present, making the present perfect passive 'has been used' appropriate.

questions.questionText: The pen is out of ink. It needs a refill. The two sentences can be combined as
options: The pen is out of ink what it needs a refill.
The pen needs a refill which is out of ink.
The pen which is out of ink needs a refill.
The pen is out of ink where it needs a refill.
questions.explanation:
The second sentence gives additional information about the pen.

 The relative pronoun 'which' can connect this information to the noun 'pen.'

 Therefore, 'The pen which is out of ink needs a refill' correctly combines the two sentences.

questions.questionText: If Lumba hadn't made the right decision, she would have been removed from her position. This is the same as
options: Lumba had made the right decision and she wasn't removed from her position.
Lumba would have been removed from her position by making the right decision.
As Lumba hadn't made the right decision, she was removed from her position.
Lumba would have been removed from her position and she had made the right decision.
questions.explanation:
This is a third conditional sentence. 

'If Lumba hadn't made the right decision, she would have been removed' describes an unreal past condition. 

It implies that, in reality, Lumba did make the right decision and therefore was not removed.

 Option A expresses this real situation.

questions.questionText: The homeroom teacher __________ some advice to his students before the final exam starts next week.
questions.explanation:
'Will have given' is the future perfect tense.

 It describes an action that will be completed before another specified event or time in the future.

 The advice will be given before the final exam starts next week, so the future perfect is appropriate.

questions.questionText: He is __________ good teacher __________ everybody respects him.
questions.explanation:
The correct structure with a singular countable noun is 'such a + adjective + noun + that.'

 Therefore, 'He is such a good teacher that everybody respects him' is grammatically correct.

 'So' is normally followed by an adjective without the noun phrase in this structure.

questions.questionText: A number of gases trap the sun's heat in the atmosphere and __________ a gradual warming of the earth.
questions.explanation:
'A number of' means several and is followed by a plural noun and plural verb.

 The subject 'a number of gases' therefore takes 'trap' and 'cause.'

 Because 'trap' and 'cause' are joined by 'and,' the correct form is 'cause.'

questions.questionText: __________ his parents come to visit him, they prefer visiting Entoto Park than going to other recreational centers.
questions.explanation:
'Whenever' means 'every time that' or 'at any time when.' 

The sentence describes a repeated situation whenever his parents come to visit him.

 Therefore, 'Whenever his parents come to visit him' is the correct expression.

questions.questionText: __________ in the USA, my sister is now living in Ethiopia with American life characteristics.
questions.explanation:
'Having grown up' is a perfect participle construction.

 It shows that growing up in the USA happened before the main action of living in Ethiopia.

 The form is 'having + past participle,' so 'having grown up' is correct.

questions.questionText: We agreed to go out for dinner __________ we didn't have food at home.
questions.explanation:
'As' can function as a conjunction meaning 'because' and introduces the reason for an action.

 They agreed to go out for dinner because there was no food at home.

 Therefore, 'as' correctly connects the two ideas.

questions.questionText: __________ he has the necessary qualification, he couldn't get a job.
questions.explanation:
'Even though' introduces a contrast or concession.

 Having the necessary qualification would normally help someone get a job, but the sentence says that he could not get one.

 Therefore, 'Even though he has the necessary qualification' is correct.

questions.questionText: My youngest brother __________ for an hour when I called him for lunch.
questions.explanation:
The past perfect continuous 'had been playing' describes an activity that started before another past event and continued for some time.

 Here, playing football continued for an hour before the speaker called him for lunch.

questions.questionText: Health and happiness are __________ money.
questions.explanation:
The sentence compares health and happiness with money.

 For a comparison between two things, the comparative structure 'more + adjective + than' is used.

 Therefore, 'more important than money' is grammatically correct.

questions.questionText: They sat on a __________ sofa.
questions.explanation:
English adjectives generally follow an order when several adjectives describe one noun.

 Opinion or quality usually comes before size, and size comes before color.

 Therefore, 'comfortable' + 'big' + 'green' gives the correct order: 'a comfortable big green sofa.'

questions.questionText: __________, they could have informed her the final decision.
questions.explanation:
'Had they seen her before' is an inverted conditional structure.

 It is equivalent to 'If they had seen her before, they could have informed her of the final decision.'

 The auxiliary 'had' is placed before the subject to form the inversion.

questions.questionText:
Reading Passage

 1. Plants reproduce by seeding. The seed of the plant contains all the necessary genetic information to create a new plant. It is designed to start growing only when the surrounding conditions are perfect. For example, the seed of a plant growing in a temperate area will \"wait\" until the cold Winter passes before growing. When Spring arrives, the seed responds to environmental triggers such as water intake, rising air temperature, humidity levels and amount of sunlight. Some seeds are programmed in such a way that they will not grow until they have passed through a period of cold weather.

2. A germinating seed will first display tiny leaves, called cotyledons. Plants are either monocotyledons, producing just a single leaf, or dicotyledons, producing two leaves. These tiny leaves quickly grow into a mature leaf system, which then begins gathering energy for the young plant. Plants gather the light of the sun and transform it into energy in a process called photosynthesis. This process allows the plant to produce glucose, which the plant then uses to both further its growth and to produce cellulose and starch. Cellulose is a strong, fibrous material that gives shape and structure to the cell walls while starch is stored in the cells and used for energy.

3. Beneath the surface, the plant's root system grows and provides not only an anchor for the plant but a constant supply of food as well. Some plants possess what is called a taproot system, in which there is one main root. Others have a more dispersed root system, which lacks a main root. In either case, the roots of the plant are covered with microscopic hairs, which spread into the surrounding soil. These hairs greatly increase the surface area of the root system and allow the plant to absorb water and essential nutrients from the soil.

4
Water drawn in through the roots undergoes a process called transpiration. During this process, minerals are carried up to the leaves of the plant, while oxygen and water vapor escape through tiny pores, called stomata, on the surface of the leaves. Interestingly, the movement of water through the plant is also responsible for keeping the plant upright; a plant that lacks water will wilt and may die. Too much water may also harm the plant by saturating the soil and preventing the roots from absorbing oxygen.5

Once a plant reaches to its full maturity, its energy is devoted to reproduction. The plant forms the two essential structures to reproduction known as flowers and fruits. The flowers of a plant are typically hermaphrodites. Thus, many plants are able to fertilize themselves. The flowers of some plants are unisexual, being all male or all female. These plants require another plant for fertilization. Some plants are polygamous. Fruits are created from the ovaries of flowering plants. The main purpose of the fruit is to protect the seed, but many fruits aid in the seed’s dispersal as well. For example, a soft, fleshy fruit attracts animals, which eat the fruit and thus spread the seeds. Some of the seeds distributed in this manner will take hold in favorable soil, and the entire process begins again."


Which one of the following is closest in meaning to the word 'dispersal' in paragraph 5?
questions.explanation:
In paragraph 5, 'dispersal' describes what happens when fruits help move seeds away from the original plant.

 The passage directly explains this by saying that animals eat the fruit and 'spread the seeds.'

 Therefore, 'spreading' is the closest meaning of 'dispersal.'

questions.questionText: Which one of the following words or phrases is similar in meaning to the word 'wilt' as used in paragraph 4?
questions.explanation:
To 'wilt' means to lose firmness and become weak, drooping, or bent, especially because of lack of water.

 The passage explains that water helps keep the plant upright and that a plant without enough water will wilt. 

Therefore, 'bend down' is the closest option.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences can be a topic sentence for paragraph 5?
options: Unisexual flowers are more capable to reproduce themselves.
Some plants are able to reproduce by themselves.
Unisexual plants require another plant to fertilize.
After maturity, plants focus on reproduction.
questions.explanation:
A topic sentence should introduce the main idea of the paragraph.

 Paragraph 5 discusses what plants do after reaching maturity, especially their reproductive structures, fertilization, flowers, fruits, and seed dispersal.

 Therefore, 'After maturity, plants focus on reproduction' gives the broadest and most accurate main idea.

questions.questionText: According to paragraph 5, unisexual flowers need another plant for fertilization because they may be
questions.explanation:
The passage states that some flowers are unisexual, meaning they are either male or female rather than containing both reproductive sexes.

 A male flower supplies pollen while a female flower receives it.

 Therefore, another plant is needed for fertilization, making 'all female or all male' the correct answer.

questions.questionText: What does the word 'This' in paragraph 2 refer to?
questions.explanation:
The sentence immediately before 'This' says that plants gather sunlight and transform it into energy in a process called 'photosynthesis.

' The next sentence says, 'This process allows the plant to produce glucose.

' Therefore, 'This' refers to photosynthesis, not cotyledon or the leaf system.

questions.questionText: What does 'It' in paragraph 1 refer to?
questions.explanation:
The first two sentences introduce 'The seed of the plant' and explain that it contains the genetic information needed to create a new plant.

 The pronoun 'It' in the next sentence refers back to this noun, meaning the seed is designed to start growing when conditions are suitable.

questions.questionText:
In paragraph 3, the writer argues that “Beneath the surface, the plant’s root system grows and provides not only an anchor for the plant but a constant supply of food as well.”
This means that the plant’s root system fundamentally serves as
options: constant supply of food for the plant.
both an anchor and a constant supply of food for the plant.
an anchor but not a constant supply of food for the plant.
an anchor for the plant that enables it absorb water from the soil.
questions.explanation:
The expression 'not only ... but ... as well' indicates two functions. 

The root system acts as an anchor that holds the plant in place and also provides a supply of water and nutrients needed by the plant.

 Therefore, the option containing both functions is correct.

questions.questionText: According to paragraph 1, which one of the following sentences is NOT true about the seeds of the plant?
options: They possess the necessary genetic inputs to produce a new plant.
few of the seeds do not grow until they have passed through a period of cold weather.
It is hard for the seeds of a plant to grow in a temperate area where there is cold Winter.
They are unable to respond to environmental triggers like rising air temperature and water intake during Spring.
questions.explanation:
The passage clearly states that seeds respond to environmental triggers such as water intake, rising air temperature, humidity, and sunlight when spring arrives.

 Therefore, the statement that seeds are unable to respond to these triggers directly contradicts the passage and is NOT true.

questions.questionText: Based on the information in paragraph 4, the process by which water comes through the roots is known as
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 4 explicitly identifies the movement of water through the plant with the process called 'transpiration.

' The other choices describe reproduction, food production, or a type of root system, so they do not fit the information in the paragraph.

questions.questionText: We cannot agree more on the decision that you have made.
options: We don't have the reason to agree on the decision you have made.
We partially agree on the decision that you have made.
We completely disagree on the decision that you have made.
We totally agree on the decision that you have made.
questions.explanation:
The expression 'cannot agree more' is an idiom meaning that there is no greater level of agreement possible.

 In other words, the speaker agrees completely or totally with the decision.

 Therefore, option D has the same meaning.

questions.questionText: Almaz was apprehensive in case the boy might sink.
options: Almaz was worried because the boy was sinking.
Almaz was bothered being tired of advising the boy.
Almaz was anxious for fear that the boy might sink.
Almaz was nervous since the boy could not be obedient.
questions.explanation:
'Apprehensive' means worried, anxious, or fearful about something that might happen.

 The phrase 'in case the boy might sink' shows that Almaz was afraid of a possible danger.

 Therefore, 'Almaz was anxious for fear that the boy might sink' expresses the same meaning.

questions.questionText: Due to poor connectivity, Gemechu could not get the director using his own mobile phone. Could you put him through to the director using the wired phone?
questions.explanation:
The phrasal verb 'put someone through' is commonly used in telephone communication.

 It means to connect a caller with another person. 

Therefore, 'put him through to the director' means 'connect him to the director.'

questions.questionText: Due to the infectious nature of the disease, the victims are segregated from the population.
questions.explanation:
'Segregated' means separated or kept apart from other people or groups.

 In this sentence, the victims are kept apart from the general population because the disease is infectious.

 Therefore, 'separated' is the closest meaning.

questions.questionText: The price of oil has been reduced by 10 percent due to the surplus production of petroleum in the Middle Eastern Countries.
questions.explanation:
'Surplus' refers to an amount that is more than what is needed or required.

 'Excess' has the same meaning. 

Therefore, 'surplus production' means production that is greater than the required amount.

questions.questionText: Hagos is very anxious to practice the tasks but he could not run away from the presentation since it weighs 20 points.
questions.explanation:
The expression 'run away from' can mean to escape or avoid something.

 In this context, Hagos cannot avoid the presentation because it carries 20 points. 

Therefore, 'escape' is the closest meaning.

questions.questionText: The matter was brought before the committee a number of times but she had a consistent opinion towards the motion.
questions.explanation:
'Consistent' means remaining the same or unchanged over time.

 The sentence says that she had the same opinion each time the matter was discussed. 

Therefore, 'the same' is the closest meaning.

questions.questionText: He was immersed in a very difficult situation but he developed a persevering stamina to overcome all irregularities.
questions.explanation:
'Persevering' describes someone who continues working toward a goal despite difficulties or obstacles.

 Such a person is determined and does not easily give up.

 Therefore, 'determined' is the closest meaning among the options.

questions.questionText: Deliberate: Accidental:: Safety: ________
questions.explanation:
'Deliberate' and 'accidental' have opposite meanings: deliberate means intentional, while accidental means unintentional. 

The analogy requires another pair of opposites.

 'Safety' means freedom from danger, while 'hazard' means a source of danger or risk.

 Therefore, 'Hazard' completes the analogy.

questions.questionText: Car: Mechanic:: Patient: ________
questions.explanation:
A mechanic is a professional who repairs or services a car. 

Similarly, a doctor is a professional who examines and treats a patient.

 Therefore, the relationship is 'Car : Mechanic :: Patient : Doctor.'

questions.questionText: The absence of an interpreter did not hinder the communication, since the team leader was a/an ____________ who could speak several languages.
questions.explanation:
'Polyglot' refers to a person who knows or can speak several languages.

 This ability makes an interpreter unnecessary in the situation described.

 'Monoglot' and 'monolingual' refer to someone who uses only one language, while an 'orator' is a skilled public speaker.

questions.questionText: As the number of pedestrians and vehicles is ____________ large on the road, special care must be taken regarding traffic rules.
questions.explanation:
'Overwhelmingly' means to a very great or considerable degree.

 The sentence emphasizes that the number of pedestrians and vehicles is extremely large, which explains why special care with traffic rules is necessary. 

Therefore, 'overwhelmingly large' is the best choice.

questions.questionText: Take care of yourself not to ____________ on the floor because she has just mopped it.
questions.explanation:
A freshly mopped floor is usually wet and can be slippery.

 When someone loses their footing on such a surface, they may 'slip.'

 Therefore, 'slip on the floor' is the correct expression.

questions.questionText: I ____________ the tourists to visit Harar Jogol as it is a historical place.
questions.explanation:
'Recommend' means to suggest that someone should do or visit something because it is considered good or worthwhile.

 Since Harar Jogol is described as a historical place, recommending tourists to visit it is logical and grammatically appropriate.

questions.questionText: Many research findings indicated that some plants could help to minimize ____________ and anxiety for cancer victims in particular.
questions.explanation:
'Depression' and 'anxiety' are both terms related to emotional and psychological well-being. 

The sentence discusses conditions that may be reduced through the benefits of some plants.

 Therefore, 'depression and anxiety' is the logical combination.

questions.questionText: Professionals specializing in History and Heritage Management have tried their level best to ____________ unique features of notable historical places by undertaking large scale research works.
questions.explanation:
'Explore' means to investigate, study, or examine something carefully in order to discover information about it.

 Since the professionals are conducting large-scale research on historical places, 'explore' is the most appropriate verb.

questions.questionText:
Reading Passage 2
The man who changed America

1 Henry Ford was born in 1863 on a farm in Dearborn, Michigan, where his English grandfather had settled after leaving Ireland in 1847. Though Henry's father was determined that his son should become a farmer, Henry had other ideas. By his early teens, he had developed a passion for mechanics and was set on becoming an engineer. Leaving home at 16, he walked to Detroit and became an apprentice, working for various employers and learning about mechanics, steam engines and, in due course, the internal combustion engine. Nevertheless, his father's influence was strong, and at the age of 23, Henry returned to Dearborn to get married and settle down on the farm his father had promised him. The agricultural interlude in his life, however, was short; and within less than two years, Ford was back in Detroit, to take up a job with the Edison Illuminating Company.\n\n2 In 1892, the first automobile was built in the United States. Within weeks, Ford, having studied the designs carefully, was hatching plans to manufacture his own horseless carriages. His first hand-built car was completed in 1896. By 1899, Ford had built three automobiles, using the profits from each one to help him refine his techniques and improve the performance of the next. In 1900, he helped to found his first car company, which failed within a year. His second venture was no more successful, and after it collapsed, Ford went back to building hand-made cars at home. Yet Ford still had ambitions to launch a company that would produce cars in a way that no other manufacturer was doing by mass production.\n\n3 It was in 1896 that Henry Ford built his first motor car. In January 1914, Henry Ford decreed that all his factory-workers should be paid at least $5 a day, for 8 hours' work. In 1913, the average paid to workers in the Ford factory had been just 2.40. But then Henry Ford was not interested in doing things the way other people said he should do them, and he was not the sort of man to stick to classic concepts and tried and trusted theories. He believed that by paying his workers more, he would get them to work better, and become better consumers.

4. Rightly, he reasoned that mass production would drastically cut production costs, and thus the price of cars. The first cars produced by the Ford Motor Company in 1903 had a price tag of $850; nevertheless, though there were plenty of prospective buyers for cars at this price, and over 1,700 were sold in the company's first year, Ford was not satisfied. He wanted to increase production to the point at which the cost of a car would fall to $500.

5. In 1907, the first “Model T” Ford emerged from Ford's factory. Its success was immediate, and within four years the company had brought a second production plant into operation. Then, in 1912, Ford introduced what was his most radical contribution to manufacturing: the moving production line. From that time onwards, instead of having workers move round a factory to work on each new vehicle, vehicles were moved round the factory on continuous lines and workers remained at fixed work stations, where each had all the tools, parts and equipment they needed. Car production was revolutionized, and by 1914, Ford boasted that his factory could build a car in 93 minutes! By 1915, over a million Model T’s had been built, and seven years later the price had fallen to under $300! By the time the vehicle went out of production in 1927, almost 16 million Model T’s had been built, and Ford had achieved his ambitions, beyond his wildest dreams               

When did Ford's company bring a second production plant of "Model T" into operation?
questions.explanation:
The passage states that the first Model T emerged in 1907 and that the company brought a second production plant into operation 'within four years.'

 Counting four years from 1907 gives 1911. 

Therefore, the correct answer is 'in 1911.'

questions.questionText: Which of the following does NOT characterize Henry Ford?
options: Being a president of a country
Being born to be an innovator
questions.explanation:
The passage presents Henry Ford as an entrepreneur, innovator, manufacturer, and someone who introduced better wages for his employees.

 However, there is no indication that he was ever the president of a country.

 Therefore, 'Being a president of a country' does NOT characterize Henry Ford.

questions.questionText: What does the word ‘venture’, in the second paragraph, mean?
questions.explanation:
In the passage, Ford's 'venture' refers to a business effort or undertaking. 

The sentence says that his second venture was unsuccessful, meaning his second attempt at establishing a successful car business failed. 

Therefore, 'attempt' is the closest meaning.

questions.questionText: What does the pronoun ‘them’ in the third paragraph refer to?
questions.explanation:
The sentence says, 'He believed that by paying his workers more, he would get them to work better.'

 The pronoun 'them' refers to the people who would receive the higher payment.

 Since the sentence directly mentions 'his workers,' 'them' refers to the workers.

questions.questionText: According to the passage, what does ‘the moving production line’ mean?
options: Workers moved round a factory to work on each new vehicle.
While workers remained at a fixed place, vehicles moved round the factory on continuous lines.
The term stands for the revolutionized nature of vehicle production.
Both vehicles and workers were moved round the factory, where each had all the tools, parts and equipment they needed.
questions.explanation:
The passage directly explains that under the moving production line, workers no longer moved around the factory with each vehicle.

 Instead, vehicles moved continuously along the production line while workers stayed at fixed workstations equipped with the necessary tools and parts.

 Therefore, option B gives the correct meaning.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following has the same meaning with the word ‘launch’ in the second paragraph?
questions.explanation:
In the context of 'launch a company,' the verb 'launch' means to start, introduce, or establish a new business.

 It does not mean to complete, install, or simply prepare something. 

Therefore, 'establish' is the closest meaning.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about Henry Ford?
options: Ford had hardly achieved his ambitions.
He believed that mass production cut production costs.
He was hard-hearted with regard to workers' payment.
In 1892, Ford had built three automobiles in the United States.
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 4 clearly states that Ford reasoned that mass production would drastically reduce production costs and consequently lower the price of cars. 

Therefore, the statement that he believed mass production cut production costs is true.

 The other options contradict information in the passage.

questions.questionText: What does the pronoun ‘it’ in the second paragraph represent?
questions.explanation:
The passage says, 'His second venture was no more successful, and after it collapsed...' The pronoun 'it' refers to the immediately preceding noun phrase 'his second venture.'

 Therefore, 'it' represents Ford's second venture.

questions.questionText: What is the overall theme of the third paragraph?
options: The revolutionizing nature of Ford’s mind about the payments of his workers
The manufacturing of Ford’s first motor car and his achievements
The average amount of payment paid to workers and their complaint
The history of payment Ford had made for his workers
questions.explanation:
Paragraph 3 focuses mainly on Ford's unusual and revolutionary decision to increase workers' wages.

 It explains that he paid workers much more than the previous average because he believed better pay would motivate them to work better and become better consumers. 

Therefore, option A best expresses the paragraph's main idea.

questions.questionText:
Selam: ____________ for the mistake I have made.

Mekides: Don't worry about it.
questions.explanation:
'Please accept my apology' is a standard and grammatically complete expression used when apologizing for a mistake.

 The phrase fits naturally before 'for the mistake I have made.'

 Therefore, the complete expression is 'Please accept my apology for the mistake I have made.'

questions.questionText:
Edilawit: I think, a person should work more than 40 hours per week.

Ruth: ____________, because that will have a negative effect on the family unit.
questions.explanation:
Ruth gives a reason that working more than 40 hours would negatively affect the family.

 This reason opposes Edilawit's suggestion, so Ruth is expressing disagreement.

 Therefore, 'I disagree with you' is the most appropriate response.

questions.questionText:
Sulamo: These days, many tourists are attracted to visit different historical places in Ethiopia. It is a good opportunity, isn't it?

Guta: Yes, it is. ____________, the local people can find jobs more easily.
questions.explanation:
'As a result' is used to introduce a consequence that follows from a previous situation.

 Increased tourism can create more employment opportunities for local people.

 Therefore, 'As a result, the local people can find jobs more easily' correctly expresses the result.

questions.questionText:
Kaba: I don't clearly understand what you mean by indigenous conflict resolution in your presentation. ____________?

Tadele: Sure, I mean, it is a traditional way of resolving conflicts.
options: Pardon me, what is your question
Can I clarify the question to you
Could you say it in another way
questions.explanation:
Kaba does not understand Tadele's explanation and wants him to express the idea differently.

 'Could you say it in another way?' is a polite request for clarification or rephrasing.

 Tadele's response then provides the meaning more clearly.

questions.questionText:
Doctor: The lab result shows that your lungs are severely affected.

Patient: Oh...doctor! What should I do to save my life?
Doctor: ____________
options: You ought to smoke cigarettes if you don't feel pain
You had better smoke cigarettes frequently
You should smoke but take care of your lung
questions.explanation:
The patient has severely affected lungs, so the appropriate advice is to avoid an activity that can further damage the lungs. Smoking cigarettes is harmful to the lungs.

 Therefore, 'You should not smoke cigarettes' is the logical and appropriate medical advice among the given options.

questions.questionText:
Director: Good morning, everyone. ____________ to attend the annual conference of our company. Can we start our discussion now?

Organizer: Yes, but firstly let me check if all the invited guests have arrived.
options: I am happy to see you
questions.explanation:
'Thank you for coming' is an appropriate expression when welcoming people who have attended an event or meeting.

 It fits naturally with 'to attend the annual conference of our company' and is suitable for the formal setting.

questions.questionText:
Fasil: Studying abroad has more advantages than disadvantages.

Fuad: ____________ studying abroad also requires a lot of money.
options: I'm afraid I can't agree with you;
questions.explanation:
'I take your point, but' is used to acknowledge someone's idea while introducing a different or opposing consideration.

 Fuad accepts that studying abroad has advantages but points out that it also requires a lot of money.

 Therefore, this expression fits the conversation.

questions.questionText:
Kibrom: Nowadays, many people die from unmanaged traffic accidents.

Hailu: ____________ The death rate is alarmingly increasing year on year.
options: I don't think it is true.
questions.explanation:
Hailu supports Kibrom's statement by adding that the death rate is increasing alarmingly every year. 

This additional statement shows strong agreement with Kibrom's opinion.

 Therefore, 'I absolutely agree with you' is the appropriate response.

questions.questionText:
Interviewer: ____________?

Interviewee: In my opinion, everybody should follow doctors' advice to halt the spread of malaria.
options: Do you think malaria is a very serious issue in our country
What do you think can people do to stop the spread of malaria
Malaria is not an important issue to waste our time on, is it
What can the government do to minimize the spread of malaria
questions.explanation:
The interviewee's answer focuses on what 'everybody' should do to stop malaria from spreading.

 Therefore, the question must ask about what people can do to stop the spread of malaria.

 Option B directly matches the information in the response.

questions.questionText:
Kaleb: Would you mind lending me your extra pen? I forgot mine at home.

Edomias: ____________. Here it is.
questions.explanation:
'Would you mind...?' is a polite way of asking for permission.

 A negative response such as 'No, I don't' means 'No, I don't mind,' which gives permission.

 The following words, 'Here it is,' confirm that Edomias is willing to lend the pen.

questions.questionText:
Samuel: Let's go to the stadium and watch football.

Bisrat: I am not a fan of football. ____________
options: My son would prefer playing football
I would rather play table tennis here
I would prefer watching football game
questions.explanation:
Bisrat says he is not a fan of football, so the next sentence should express an alternative preference.

 'I would rather play table tennis here' means he prefers playing table tennis instead of going to watch football.

 Therefore, option C fits the context.

questions.questionText:
Traffic Police: Do you know the purpose of zebra crossing?

Driver: ____________. It is designed for pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation:
The question begins with 'Do you know...?' and asks whether the driver knows the purpose of a zebra crossing.

 The correct positive short answer is 'Yes, I do.' 

The following sentence then explains its purpose: it is designed for pedestrians to cross.

questions.questionText:
Chairperson: Our organization needs a major reform to cope with the existing global challenges.

Participant: ____________, we have to follow the model of other organizations that have survived the crises and are now successful in their business.
options: It is a good point but
questions.explanation:
'I get your point' means 'I understand what you are saying.'

 It naturally introduces the participant's response to the chairperson's idea before suggesting that the organization should learn from successful organizations.

 Therefore, it is the most appropriate expression.

questions.questionText:
Gebre: Why did you go to the bazaar yesterday?

Obang: ____________.
options: To buy some shoes and clothes for my children
Because I wanted to study for my exam
In order to discuss with the bank manager
questions.explanation:
A bazaar is a marketplace where people commonly go to buy goods.

 Among the choices, buying shoes and clothes for the children is the most natural reason for visiting a bazaar.

 Therefore, option A is the best answer.

questions.questionText:
Bereket: When visiting a foreign country, it is important to know how to be polite in that culture.

Melkamu: Sure! ____________ I say we should learn in school about the customs of other countries.
questions.explanation:
'That's why' introduces a conclusion or reason based on the previous statement.

 Bereket says that understanding other cultures is important, and Melkamu uses that idea to conclude that schools should teach students about other countries' customs.

 Therefore, 'That's why' fits the relationship between the ideas.

questions.questionText:
Senait: What is new, Tolasa? You seem surprised!

Tolasa: ____________, I have met my mother after 27 years of longing.
questions.explanation:
'Funnily enough' is an expression used to introduce something surprising or unexpected.

 Meeting his mother after 27 years is an extraordinary and unexpected event in the context, so the expression naturally introduces Tolasa's surprising news.

questions.questionText:
Robera: I have just heard that one of our colleagues passed away accidentally.

Ashebir: ____________! I really feel sad to hear that.
questions.explanation:
'What a pity!' is an expression used to show sadness, sympathy, or regret when hearing unfortunate news.

 Since Ashebir has learned that a colleague has died, this expression appropriately communicates sorrow.

questions.questionText:
Mohammed: Glad to meet you, Hanan. What do you do during the summer vacation?

Hanan: Glad to meet you, too. ____________
options: I read novels to improve my English.
Summer season is rainy, isn't it?
I sometimes go to school with my friends.
questions.explanation:
Mohammed asks Hanan what she does during the summer vacation, so the response should describe a vacation activity.

 'I read novels to improve my English' directly answers the question by giving an activity she does during the vacation.

questions.questionText:
Edom: ____________, Megarsa. I thank you very much on behalf of our organization.

Megarsa: It is my regular duty, Madam.
options: You have done a great job
What a nice car you have
What a lovely office you have
questions.explanation:
Edom is thanking Megarsa on behalf of the organization, so the missing expression should relate to his work or performance.

 'You have done a great job' is an appropriate compliment for someone's successful work and fits Megarsa's reply that it is his regular duty.

questions.questionText:
Mengistu: How do you think schools should manage disciplinary problems?

Berhane: I think ____________ because the ultimate purpose of schools is to produce responsible citizens.
options: the school shouldn't bother about it
the government should take corrective measures
the school should set a strict code of conducts
the school should expel students who behave well
questions.explanation:
Schools need clear rules and standards to manage student behavior and encourage responsibility.

 A strict code of conduct establishes expectations and helps students understand acceptable behavior.

 Therefore, option C is the most reasonable and constructive answer.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following elements in a formal letter carries the writer's address and date?
questions.explanation:
The heading of a formal letter normally contains the writer's address and the date.

 The salutation is the greeting, the body contains the main message, and the closing contains the complimentary close and signature.

 Therefore, 'Heading' is correct.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic of a formal letter?
options: formal letter is written using friendly terms.
The tone of a formal letter should be respectful.
We can use jargons in writing a formal letter.
We can use inconsistent structure in writing a formal letter.
questions.explanation:
A formal letter is used for official, professional, academic, or other serious communication.

 Therefore, its language should be polite, respectful, clear, and appropriately formal.

 An inconsistent structure or overly casual language is not normally suitable.

questions.questionText:
I was pleased to hear from you after a long time. Just before two days, our intimate friend Selam said 'I wonder what's happened to Melaku!'"
From which type of letter writing, the above two lines are most likely extracted?
questions.explanation:
The passage uses a personal and friendly tone, mentions an intimate friend, and discusses personal communication between people who know each other.

 These are typical characteristics of an informal letter. 

Therefore, 'An informal letter writing' is correct.

questions.questionText:
Section Two: Punctuation and Capitalization
Choose the statement which is correctly punctuated and capitalized:
options: I study French every monday, wednesday and friday from January to May.
I study french every Monday, Wednesday and Friday from january to may.
I study french every monday, wednesday and friday from january to may.
I study French every Monday, Wednesday and Friday from January to May.
questions.explanation:
Proper capitalization is required for names of languages, days, and months. 

'French' is a language name, while 'Monday,' 'Wednesday,' 'Friday,' 'January,' and 'May' are names of days and months. 

All of them must begin with capital letters.

 Therefore, option D is correctly capitalized and punctuated.

questions.questionText: Choose the statement which is correctly punctuated and capitalized:
questions.explanation:
A direct quotation beginning a complete sentence should start with a capital letter.

 The reporting clause 'Our English teacher said' is followed by a comma before the quotation.

 The full stop is placed inside the quotation marks in this sentence. 

Therefore, option B is correctly punctuated and capitalized.

questions.questionText: Choose the statement which is correctly punctuated and capitalized:
options: Hanna the grandmother of Begna, is visited every Sunday.
Hanna, the grandmother of Begna is visited every Sunday.
Hanna, the grandmother of Begna is visited, every Sunday.
Hanna, the grandmother of Begna, is visited every Sunday.
questions.explanation:
'The grandmother of Begna' is additional information identifying Hanna and functions as a non-defining appositive phrase.

 Because it is additional information, it must be enclosed by commas on both sides.

 Therefore, the correct sentence is 'Hanna, the grandmother of Begna, is visited every Sunday.'

questions.questionText: a/ committee/ elected/ he/ as/ chairperson / was/ of/ the.
options: He was elected as a chairperson of the committee.
chairperson of the committee was he elected as.
As a chairperson of the committee, he was elected.
The chairperson was elected as a committee of he.
questions.explanation:
Option A places the words in the correct grammatical order: subject 'He' + passive verb 'was elected' + complement 'as a chairperson' + phrase 'of the committee.

' The resulting sentence is clear and grammatically acceptable.

questions.questionText: was/park/saw/a/in/I/jogging /tortoise/I/while/the.
options: In the park, I saw a tortoise, while was I jogging.
While I was jogging in the park, I saw a tortoise.
I saw a tortoise, while was I jogging in the park.
In the park, a tortoise saw I while I was jogging.
questions.explanation:
Option B correctly forms a complex sentence.

 The time clause 'While I was jogging in the park' contains the subject 'I' followed by the past continuous verb 'was jogging.

' The main clause 'I saw a tortoise' then gives the event that happened during the activity.

questions.questionText: Ethiopia/ groups/ mutual/ among/ grown/ various/ respect/ ethnic/ is/ a/ home/ in/ practice.
options: home-grown practice in Ethiopia respect ethnic groups mutual is among various.
Mutual respect among various ethnic groups is a home-grown practice in Ethiopia.
home-grown practice in Ethiopia is respect among various ethnic mutual groups.
Ethiopia is mutual respect among various ethnic groups a practice in home-grown.
questions.explanation:
Option B correctly organizes the words into a grammatical sentence.

 The subject is 'Mutual respect among various ethnic groups,' followed by the linking verb 'is' and the complement 'a home-grown practice in Ethiopia.'

 The sentence is both grammatically correct and meaningful.

questions.questionText:
a. The moon, in fact, is much smaller than the sun, but it is also a great deal closer to the earth.

b. A solar eclipse is an astronomical event during which the moon seems to cover the sun.

c. As a result, both the sun and the moon seem to be about the same size to us.

d. When the moon passes between the earth and the sun, all or part of the sun's light is blotted out.
questions.explanation:
Sentence (b) should come first because it introduces the topic of a solar eclipse. 

Sentence (d) then explains what happens during an eclipse when the moon passes between the earth and the sun. 

Sentence (a) explains why the smaller moon can appear large enough to cover the sun: it is much closer to Earth.

 Finally, (c) begins with 'As a result,' so it logically concludes the explanation. 

Therefore, the order is b-d-a-c.

questions.questionText:
a. In light of this, online education is a hub of learning in the twenty-first century.

b. To begin with, online learning has provided learners a lot of opportunities, including getting resources easily.

c. Students can also make learning a reality while they are in far places, convenient for distance learners.

d. Compared to the traditional mode of learning, online learning has come up with a number of advantages for learners.
questions.explanation:
Sentence (d) introduces the general idea that online learning has advantages over traditional learning. 

Sentence (b) then gives the first advantage, signaled by 'To begin with.' Sentence (c) adds another advantage using 'also.'

 Sentence (a) concludes with 'In light of this,' referring to the advantages already discussed.

 Therefore, the correct order is d-b-c-a.

questions.questionText:
a. Regular physical exercise has contributed a lot for mental well-being.

b. In view of this, people should develop the habit of doing physical exercise.

c. When people are engaged in activities like swimming and running, their bodies release endorphin that reduces the feeling of tension.

d. In addition to this, doing regular physical exercise enables people to be alert and conscious.
questions.explanation:
Sentence (a) introduces the main idea that regular physical exercise benefits mental well-being. 

Sentence (c) explains one way exercise helps by describing the release of endorphins. 

Sentence (d) adds another benefit using 'In addition to this.' 

Finally, (b) gives a recommendation based on the information, introduced by 'In view of this.'

 Therefore, the correct order is a-c-d-b.

questions.questionText:
a. First, the majority of houses in poor villages and urban slums are not yet served by a piped water system.

b. There are several reasons for this.

c. People living in these places often have to walk many miles to find water and carry it home in jugs and plastic containers.

d. In developing countries, poor people suffer the most from shortage of water.
questions.explanation:
Sentence (d) introduces the main problem: poor people in developing countries suffer greatly from water shortages.

 Sentence (b) follows naturally by saying that there are several reasons for this problem.

 Sentence (a) introduces the first reason with 'First,' and sentence (c) explains the difficulty faced by people living in those areas.

 Therefore, the correct sequence is d-b-a-c.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sentences can be topic sentence?
options: Watching less television can still help children get better grades.
Children who are keen readers may get much better grades than their peers.
Parents play an important role in their children’s academic success.
Video games have also a negative impact on children’s academic success.
questions.explanation:
A topic sentence should introduce the main idea broadly enough to allow several supporting details to follow.

 'Parents play an important role in their children’s academic success' is broad and can be supported by different examples about parents' influence.

 The other choices describe specific effects or activities, making them more suitable as supporting details.

questions.questionText:
Some classroom disruptions are routine and minor; others are severe and intolerable. Disruptiveness may be caused by boredom, frustration, peer recognition for being a hero or deeper problems of poverty, alienation, low ability, irrelevant curriculum, impersonal schools or peer traditions of defiance. A few students will have severe problems, including psychosis.
Which of the following sentences is most likely considered as a topic sentence of the above paragraph?
options: Disruptiveness lies in preventing trouble before it happens.
Disruptiveness is a regular practice observed in every classroom in the school compound.
Students' disruptiveness has different levels and can result from different factors.
There are so many psychological factors students face in their classroom.
questions.explanation:
The paragraph discusses two main ideas: classroom disruptiveness can have different levels, from minor to severe, and it can result from many different causes such as boredom, frustration, poverty, alienation, and low ability.

 Option C covers both major ideas, so it is the best topic sentence.

questions.questionText:
Kindheartedness and generosity are the real colors of Boja's behavior. He is helpful in every spectrum of life and he has a kind heart for all creatures. When he gets a destitute on the street, he gives his lunch. He is so kind that he hurts himself by helping others.
This is a piece of writing that is most likely ____________.
questions.explanation:
The paragraph mainly describes Boja's character, behavior, and qualities.

 It gives examples of his kindness, generosity, and willingness to help others.

 Since the purpose is to describe a person rather than tell a sequence of events, argue a position, or explain causes and effects, it is descriptive writing.

questions.questionText:
Section Six: Word Spelling
Choose the word which is correctly spelt:
questions.explanation:
'Malnutrition' is correctly spelled and means poor health caused by an inadequate or unbalanced intake of nutrients.

 The other words contain spelling errors: 'expresion' should be 'expression,' 'justifecation' should be 'justification,' and 'endaevour' should be 'endeavour.'

 Therefore, 'malnutrition' is correct.

questions.questionText: Choose the word which is correctly spelt:
questions.explanation:
'Autonomous' is correctly spelled and means having the freedom or ability to govern or control oneself.

 The other words are misspelled: 'Inclussive' should be 'Inclusive,' 'Setlement' should be 'Settlement,' and 'Hazarduos' should be 'Hazardous.'

 Therefore, 'Autonomous' is the correctly spelled word.
